name: MassOptions (Executive Office of Aging & Independence)
description: MassOptions is Massachusetts’ free statewide line for older adults, people with disabilities and caregivers. It connects callers to their local Aging Services Access Point and Area Agency on Aging for home care, meals, caregiver support and options counseling.
next_step: Call and describe what is hard right now. Ask for information and assistance. Ask MassOptions for the elder services agency that serves your city or town. Military service is not required.
constraints: Many services focus on people age 60 and older and adults with disabilities; eligibility and waitlists vary by program.
Statewide; MassOptions refers you to the elder services agency for your city or town.

source_evidence.title: Executive Office of Aging & Independence: Aging Support for Older Adults in Massachusetts
source_evidence.scope: Call MassOptions at 1-800-243-4636 to get connected to local services; search excerpt. Massachusetts organizes aging services by city and town through Area Agencies on Aging and Aging Services Access Points; MassOptions refers callers to their local elder services agency (https://www.mass.gov/info-details/services; search excerpt). Every county shows the statewide line.

name: Massachusetts Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program
description: The regional long-term care ombudsman for this county: advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and residential care facilities.
next_step: Call the regional ombudsman program. Give the facility name and county. For immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing or enforcement agency.
The state line connects you to the local ombudsman program for the facility’s city or town.

source_evidence.title: Executive Office of Aging & Independence: Ombudsman Programs
source_evidence.scope: Long-Term Care Ombudsman support is free for residents of nursing homes, rest homes and assisted living; call (617) 222-7495 to connect with your local ombudsman; search excerpt. Local programs are listed by city and town (https://www.mass.gov/info-details/find-an-ombudsman-representative-for-a-nursing-or-rest-home), so every county shows the state line.
